Hi Neha / Camila / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ForgeIT is excited about building a tighter integration to ship out a bundled offering next quarter. Two quick asks as we scope commercial terms so we can finalize our internal forecasts: 

1) Attribution model: how does Redwood intend to attribute first-touch vs last-touch for partner-originated revenue in the partner catalog? Our FP team needs clarity on whether the partner gets the referral credit for a demo or only after a signed deal.

2) Revenue-hold / escrow: for co-sell deals where there is variable pass-through (implementation fees, usage adjustments), is Redwood open to a 60-day escrow before remitting gross rev share?

I've attached a short overview (forgeit-intro.pdf) and copied Liam (commercial lead). Can you share a proposed policy matrix (demo credit, trial conversion window, escrow hold, exceptions)? If it helps, we can do a 30-minute sync next week.

Subject: Re: Partner catalog fingerprinting & first-touch allocation model

Hi Amelia — great to hear, and congrats on the momentum. Quick pass below with a pragmatic baseline we use for partners + a few optional guardrails. Attaching a lightweight spreadsheet to illustrate the waterfall (partner-catalog-draft.xlsx).

Baseline proposal (for catalog-listed ISV integrations):
- Fingerprinting: catalog entries get a stable partner ID (catalog fingerprint). Attribution is assigned by partner ID when the user originates from the partner listing or a partner-managed demo link.
- First-touch window: partner receives referral credit if the customer signs within 45 days of the first tracked interaction that can be tied to the partner fingerprint (demo, lead form, trial activation).
- Demo credits: we offer a one-time demo credit (value capped at $2,000 equivalent) to offset initial trial/proof-of-concept costs — requires a recorded demo or joint session.
- Escrow / holdback: for revenue-share on usage-based contracts we hold 60 days of gross proceeds to reconcile usage adjustments; remits monthly thereafter. We can shorten to 30 days for strategic pilots with executive sponsor approval.
- Exceptions & clawback: if a partner attempts to game attribution (synthetic leads, self-referrals), we reserve the right to claw back credits for 12 months.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review spreadsheet for commission waterfall and sample calculations.
2) If this baseline looks acceptable, our legal team will draft a short MSA addendum (partner catalog appendix) to attach to the standard reseller/referral schedule.
3) Agree on registration window process (HubSpot form + DOC link) — we usually require claim within 7 days of first demo to seed priority.

If you want to tighten anything (e.g., 30d vs 45d window, different escrow), list priorities and we can run trade-offs. I can meet Tue or Wed afternoon PT.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Adding a couple of implementation items from ops/finance perspective:

- Commission waterfall (prototype in attached spreadsheet): 1) partner first-touch credit; 2) partner co-sell split if Redwood sales materially influenced close (tracked via deal stages and SFDC flag); 3) residual usage share.
- Lead registration window: we support the 45-day first-touch but require partner to submit the registration via the HubSpot form within 7 days of demo; registration timestamps populate the fingerprint metadata.
- Escrow mechanics: recommend 60-day hold for usage invoices with monthly reconciliation reports — Finance will produce a clearsheet and remittances on the 15th of each month.

I uploaded a draft partner-catalog-draft.xlsx to the shared drive (see link in the thread metadata). If everyone is aligned I can loop Legal to prepare an addendum that covers the escrow and clawback language.

—Ben

Thanks — this looks sensible and addresses the key questions we had. A few confirmations from our side: 

- 45-day first-touch is acceptable (we'll prioritize early registration to protect the lead).
- 60-day escrow standard is fine for initial launch; we'll request 30-day for the pilot after we hit $X M ARR if we get an executive exception.
- Demo credit cap of $2k is workable.

Can Legal prepare the MSA addendum and send a DocuSign envelope? Also please include the HubSpot registration form fields so our sales ops can pre-populate the partner flow.

If we can get the addendum into DocuSign this week, ForgeIT can sign and push to our onboarding checklist.

Best,
